help.title: Help & Videos
help.subtitle: How Kisan Mitra works, what each check means, and what is not available yet.
help.gettingStartedHint: Six short steps cover the whole app. Open any step to go straight to that screen.

diagnose.title: Check a crop leaf
diagnose.body: Photograph a single affected leaf on a plain background and upload it with the crop you are growing. JPEG, PNG and WebP up to 5 MB are accepted. You get an AI-assisted prediction with a confidence score and a quality check on the photo. The model only knows a limited set of crops — for anything else the app says so instead of guessing.

prices.title: Look up mandi prices
prices.body: Search a commodity and narrow by state and district. Rows show the arrival date, minimum, maximum and modal price, and the source. Prices come from data.gov.in (AGMARKNET). When live data is unavailable, rows are clearly marked as sample prices and never presented as today's market rate.

listProduce.title: List your produce for sale
listProduce.body: Add a listing with crop, quantity, unit and an optional price, then review enquiries in one place. Contact details stay hidden until you accept an enquiry; only then is your phone number shared with that buyer. You can close a listing once the produce is sold.

reminders.title: Set farm reminders
reminders.body: Create reminders for irrigation, fertiliser or spraying, with a due date, and link one to a saved crop if you like. Due items appear on your dashboard. The advice page does not read weather data — it works from your crops and reminders only.

assistant.title: Ask the AI assistant
assistant.body: Ask short questions about crop care, your own check results, prices or schemes in English or Hindi. The assistant answers only from records it can reach for your role and shows its evidence. When a question is outside that scope it says so and suggests who to ask instead.

schemes.title: Check government schemes
schemes.body: Every published scheme shows who it is for, what it offers, its official link and the date the details were last verified. Always read the official page before applying — the app does not process applications and does not publish dates that were not verified.

market.title: Find produce to buy
market.body: Browse open listings and filter by crop, state and district. Send an enquiry with the quantity you need and a short message. The farmer's phone number is shown only after they accept your enquiry; once accepted you can also rate the transaction.

admin.title: Manage content and users
admin.body: The admin console is where schemes, farm updates and knowledge-base articles are created, edited and withdrawn. It also lists users by role and listings by status so you can review what is published.

schemesReview.title: Verify what you publish
schemesReview.body: Schemes carry an official URL and a last-verified date, and the app shows both. Re-verify eligibility and benefit wording at the official source before each update, and unpublish anything that is out of date.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.badge: Answers from how the app works
faq.hint: These answers describe what this build actually does. Tap a question to expand it.

photos.q: What kind of photo should I upload for a crop check?
photos.a: One leaf, filling most of the frame, on a plain background, in even light. JPEG, PNG and WebP are accepted up to 5 MB. A photo that is too large, in another format, too blurry or too dark is rejected with a reason rather than being analysed. If no diagnosis model is available, the check returns an error instead of a guess.

accuracy.q: Is the diagnosis a confirmed result?
accuracy.a: No. It is an AI-assisted prediction. The app shows the confidence score, the status (for example low confidence or unsupported crop) and a quality report for the photo. Treat it as a pointer, and confirm with an agriculture extension officer or another qualified expert before applying any treatment.

reports.q: How is the crop report produced?
reports.a: Reports are generated from your check. When the language model is configured they are AI-assisted from verified sources; otherwise a verified template is used. Either way the report lists what was found, symptoms to check, recommended actions and safety notes. Reports are available in English and Hindi and are saved once generated.

prices.q: Where do mandi prices come from?
prices.a: From data.gov.in (AGMARKNET), and each row shows its arrival date and source. When live data cannot be reached the app falls back to clearly labelled sample prices marked “not live” — those are for demonstration only and are never present as today's rate. Always confirm with your local mandi.

contact.q: When can I see the farmer's phone number?
contact.a: Only after the farmer accepts your enquiry. Until then the listing shows no contact details. Farmers' numbers are never shown publicly. After an accepted enquiry the buyer can leave a one-time rating from 1 to 5 stars.

roles.q: What can each kind of account do?
roles.a: Farmers save crops, run leaf checks, create listings, respond to enquiries and set reminders. Buyers browse listings, send enquiries, rate an accepted deal and view prices and schemes. Admins manage schemes, updates, the knowledge base and review users and listings. The assistant is available to every signed-in role, but answers are limited to what that role may see.

assistant.q: What can the AI assistant answer?
assistant.a: Questions it can ground in data you are allowed to see: your check results, market prices, published schemes, and generally available guidance. It shows the evidence it used and asks a follow-up when the question is unclear. It cannot change records or open new pages for you — it suggests the screen to use instead.

language.q: How do I switch between English and Hindi?
language.a: Use the language buttons at the bottom of the sidebar. The choice is saved on this device. The interface, crop reports and assistance follow that language; the assistant also answers in the language you write in when it supports it.

status.title: System status
status.hint: Read live from the backend readiness check. These are the three services this app depends on.
status.dbDetail: Stores your account, crops, checks and listings.
status.modelFailDetail: Leaf checks will return an error until the model is available.
status.llmOkDetail: Assistant answers and reports can use the language model.
status.llmOffDetail: The assistant reports a fallback mode; reports use verified templates.
status.offlineNote: If the check failed, try again in a moment. Your data is not affected.
status.footnote: Status shows only what the backend reports. A green badge means the service answered this check — not a guarantee of ongoing availability.

videos.state: Video walkthroughs are not published yet
videos.body: We are not linking to third-party videos or placeholder clips. For now, the numbered steps above cover the same ground in writing, with a direct link to each screen.
videos.request: A Hindi and English walkthrough is planned. Until then, ask your agriculture extension officer to show you the first crop check.

support.title: Getting help
support.body: In-app support tickets are not available in this version. Nothing you send here would reach a person, and there is no support inbox to check.
support.extension: For farm problems, contact your local agriculture extension officer or Krishi Vigyan Kendra — they can look at the crop in person, which an app cannot. For scheme questions, read the official link shown on each scheme before applying.
